request: Allow multiple Special Item requests to share existing Sales Orders and Purchase Orders.
specApproval: not obtained (autonomous run; user authorized the behavior change)
behaviors: Two or more Special cases can manually link the same SO, PO, or SO/PO pair, including through the existing Sales and SCM HTTP routes.
Concurrent links by different cases both succeed and preserve each case's own lines, revision, and link event.
A case cannot overwrite its existing SO or PO with a different order; stale revisions, order identity validation, role authorization, and yard scope remain enforced.
Order-operation IDs remain unique even though order references may be shared.
An SO or PO webhook updates every linked Special case in ascending request ID order, including status, revision, reconciliation event, audit result, and UI update notification.
A line-reconciliation problem in one linked case records attention for that case while other linked cases continue to reconcile.
Unmatched webhooks and single-case result fields remain compatible, and existing Backorder sharing behavior is preserved.
The migration preserves existing rows and audit records and replaces only order-owner uniqueness with non-unique lookup indexes. Transactional migration rollback is rehearsed.

failureModel.partialOrStaleUpdates: Multi-case webhook regression and attention isolation tests.
failureModel.concurrentLinkConflictOrOverwrite: Actual concurrent database transactions plus same-case stale-revision checks.
failureModel.authorizationRegression: Sales/SCM HTTP role and yard tests.
failureModel.dataLossOrWrongIndexRemoved: Migration row snapshots, index inspection, operation-ID collision checks, and rollback rehearsal.

setup.git: Keep the existing dirty worktree; capture task-local baseline files. No commits or changes to unrelated edits.
setup.tools: Existing Node test runner, fast-check, c8, ESLint, TypeScript, and an available cached test image.
setup.tests: Repository standard isolated Compose configuration under mbbs-tests.slice, bounded CPU/memory/PIDs/tmpfs, teardown registered before launch.
setup.evidence: Persist baseline, RED/GREEN logs, source hashes, final regression results, mutation checks, static checks, changed-line coverage, and cleanup verification.
setup.release: Prepare a scoped candidate on each current app/worker image, preserve runtime configuration and rollback artifacts, and verify the deployed source and health.

limits: No order creation, cancellation, quantities, pricing, or Dispatch allocation semantics are changed by this task.
